text:
T.J. Hughes went undrafted, played at Michigan through last season at 57 points in 40 games, and has been a regular in Colorado from the start of his first NHL season: 21 games, about 15 minutes a night, and power-play time with four points there.

He's in an odd spot. He has a four-game point streak, all assists, and he hasn't scored in 12 games despite 4.0 expected goals in that stretch. For the season it's two goals on 6.0 expected, 4.2% shooting against a range closer to 11%. The looks are real, and goals usually follow looks.

The concern is at five on five, where the Avalanche get 48% of the expected goals with him on, more than five points worse than without him. That's normal for a rookie still learning to defend at this level, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has only six of his games so far, with nothing yet standing out either way. The Colorado Springs Gazette has written about how he can stick long term. The finishing coming around would help that case most.
